title: Schools attended and music in school
summary: Lists his New Orleans schools and says school music was minor; he missed borrowing a trumpet, which pushed him to play.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Well did you go to public school here in the city entirely? Yeah, I went to public school, yeah.
Well that's quite a long time ago.
Which schools did you go to?

Well I went to, when we first moved to New Orleans, I started at Live Oak, which is now a high school I understand. It was a grammar school then. And then we naturally moved around town until we finally found a neighborhood they liked, you know. And then I went to McDonough 18 for just what, about a year, and then we moved again. So I went to Benjamin Franklin, which is now a colored school. And I graduated from there, from eighth grade, then went to Warren Easton.
What kind of music did they have in the schools in those days?

There wasn't too much of a, I mean music wasn't a big thing in schools in those days, you know. They had a music class and they used to lend the instruments to the pupils, to the students. And I went to borrow a trumpet and I was too late, I'd just given out the last one. So that's when I made up my mind that I definitely had to play music. You know, I could taste it. And one thing I can say that I've done the thing I like to do all my life. I mean I'd rather play music than anything else I guess.
That's wonderful you can do it.
